answer: reputation by completing small, paid, verifiable tasks in a beacon epoch, where a beacon coordinator hashes completed work into a public tide of contributions that everyone can audit. Trust weight rises with accumulated work, and new identities inherit nothing. The cost to an attacker is brutal: to make one fake identity worth enough to matter in votes or payouts, it must actually perform the same scarce work, and the payout pool pays less per unit than the tasks cost in compute and time, so mass-registration of cheap identities yields thousands of worthless zero-weight accounts.
